title: Gotchas
description: The mistakes calimero-sdk apps make most often, each with the rule that avoids it.
sidebar:
  order: 30
---

The short list. Each item links to the page that explains it.

## Numbers and arguments

- `u64`, `i64` and `Vec<u8>` travel as decimal strings and base64url, in
  arguments, results, record fields, errors and events. A client sends
  `{"size": "7"}`, not `{"size": 7}`.
- The same types nested in another type (`Vec<u64>`, `Option<Vec<i64>>`) do not
  compile: wrap them in a `Record` or send strings
  ([SDK macros](/build/sdk-macros/#applogic)).
- A `u64` inside your own plain serde struct reaches JSON as a number, which
  JavaScript may round. Use a `Record`, whose derive converts it; on a
  `#[derive(AbiType)]` type, give the field its D20 helper or mark it
  `#[abi(plain)]` so the ABI says it is a number (unmarked, it does not compile;
  [SDK macros](/build/sdk-macros/#deriveabitype)).
- Arguments are camelCase (`room_id` → `roomId`), and unknown keys are refused
  (`BadArgs`).

## State

- Renaming a state field or changing its type orphans its data: an upgrade keeps
  the state and has no migration step ([Upgrades & state](/build/migrations/)).
- A record must not also derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize`: `#[derive(Record)]`
  writes them.
- Uniqueness belongs in the key or a `unique(..)` constraint, not in a check
  before an insert.
- Prefer `env::unique_id()` to a `Counter` for ids.
- Multi-row reads are pages of at most 1,000; follow `next`
  ([Tables & Collections](/build/collections/)).

## Access

- A method with no attribute admits any signed-in account the node lets reach
  the app; org membership is the app's to check with `guards`
  ([Access control](/build/guides/access-control/)).
- Take the caller from `env::caller()` or a guard, never from an argument.
- `#[app::error]` and `#[app::event]` must be in the `#[app::logic]` module, or
  the ABI lists none of them. Every field needs a name: `Invalid(String)` does
  not compile, `Invalid { reason: String }` does.
- Every app is in an organization (a personal one when created without one), and
  a cross-app call reaches only apps in the same organization.

## Runs

- A call that fails writes nothing and emits nothing; a panic is a trap, not an
  app error ([Error handling](/build/error-handling/)).
- `env::xcall` only queues a message: it is delivered after the entry commits,
  and only if the run succeeds ([Cross-app calls](/build/guides/cross-context/)).
- Only views may search; a call that searches traps
  ([Search](/build/guides/search/)).
- `env::fetch`, actions and cross-app calls answer an error on the host target;
  test them with `TestApp` ([Testing](/build/testing/)).
- A **read-only** team member reaches an app's views only: a call to any other
  method is refused with `403` before it runs.
- `files::open` works only inside an `#[app::compute]` run; a call or view gets
  a file's size and hash from `BlobRef::info` ([Files and blobs](/build/guides/blobs/)).

## Build and ship

- An SDK 0.12 app (a WASM core module, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`) is refused at
  upload and install (`400 UNSUPPORTED_BUNDLE`); one left over from before
  answers `410 UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE`. Rebuild on `calimero-sdk` for
  `wasm32-wasip2` with `meroctl app build`.
- Sign every release of a package with the same key: another key is another
  application, not an upgrade ([Packaging & signing](/build/packaging-signing/)).
- Bump `#[app::state(version = N)]` with every state change; `meroctl app sign
  --previous` (and `meroctl app pack --previous`) refuses a removed or retyped state field without it.
